g.text: 🐘 APACHE HADOOP, SPARK & ECOSYSTEM UNIFIED BIG DATA PLATFORM
Distributed HDFS • YARN • Apache Spark 3.5 • Hive • Sqoop • Oozie • Pig • JupyterLab Studio • Unified Platform Console (:3030)
Enterprise Production-Grade Big Data Stack • Single Pane of Glass Management
Hadoop + Spark + Hive + Jupyter + Control Hub
Ephemeral clusters • GCS (gs://) • Spot workers • Gateway
Kali Rolling • Hadoop 3.3.6 • 6GB RAM / 4 vCPUs • G1GC
Ubuntu 24.04 • 4 vCPUs • Dynamic RAM • UEFI CA • NAT fix
Windows 11 Native Kernel • xRDP Port 3390 • Zero VM lag
Central dashboard, Web UIs & Interactive Studios
Boots Hadoop + Spark + Hub & auto-opens browser
Provisions GCP Dataproc & Compute Engine VM
Calibrates VMX specs & boots Kali Workstation
DataFrame CSV ingestion & Snappy Parquet write
Relational SQL queries & Hive catalog integration
Engineers submit Spark applications, Hive queries, or MR jobs
via Control Hub (:3030), JupyterLab (:8888), or Spark RPC (:7077).
HDFS: 3.1.2 | SPARK: 3.5.1 | HIVE: Metastore | JAVA: OpenJDK 8/11 | BRIDGE NET: bigdata-net
Cluster Namespace Coordinator • Inodes Tree in RAM
Holds HDFS directory tree, file-to-block map, quotas, and WebHDFS REST endpoints
and block metadata serialized on disk
State Consolidation & Checkpointing Engine (Prevents Bloated Edits)
Periodically pulls fsimage and edits via HTTP, merges them in RAM, and ships
the fresh checkpoint image back to the Active NameNode for instant reboots.
Pull [fsimage + edits] ➔ Merge in Memory ➔ Push [fsimage.ckpt] ➔ Roll Edits
Physical Distributed Block Storage & Integrity Verification
If heartbeat missing for 10 minutes (600s), NameNode marks DataNode dead and
triggers automatic under-replicated block healing to surviving worker nodes.
Incoming data chunked into 128MB chunks. Writes stream
over Data Transfer Protocol (:9866). Inodes recorded in NameNode
WAL (edits) and committed to durable named Docker volumes.
In-Memory DAG Execution • Distributed Spark Workers
Builds execution DAG of stages, optimizes shuffles, dispatches tasks to Worker Executors
Capacity Scheduler • 3072 MB Total Dynamic Memory Pool
🎯 Multi-Engine Orchestration: Spark on YARN & MapReduce
Supports both standalone Spark and YARN client/cluster submissions (spark-submit --master yarn).
Allocates 512MB slot containers with low-pause G1GC tuning.
Archives completed tasks, aggregated container logs, and diagnostic counters.
Spark Master launches worker executors, while YARN allocates
isolated container slots with strict memory guards (512MB default).
Data locality reads 128MB HDFS blocks directly from local DataNode.
Predicate pushdown, column pruning & 100x faster than MR
SQL over HDFS Storage & HiveServer2 JDBC:
Schemas, partitions, and relational analytics over Big Data
• Spark tasks run in executor memory (100x faster than disk).
• Intermediate key-values partitioned and shuffled across network.
• Reducers aggregate and sort grouped datasets.
Aggregated Parquet or CSV output written back to
HDFS DataNode (or GCS gs:// bucket on Dataproc).
Status verified: SUCCESS across all pipeline stages.
Zero Data Loss: Named Docker Volumes, Spark Event Logs & Cloud Storage (gs://)
Filesystem namespace tree, fsimage snapshots, and edits WAL
Raw 128MB replicated data blocks (blk_* and blk_*.meta checksums)
Spark DAG event logs • Picked up by Spark History Server (:18080)
Shuffle spills, temporary intermediate buffers, and cloud staging
Persisted PySpark pipelines, Jupyter notebooks, and dataset artifacts
UNIFIED BIG DATA ARCHITECTURE SPECIFICATIONS SUMMARY:
• HDFS Block Size: 128 MB | Spark Standalone: 7077/8080 | Hive Warehouse: /user/hive/warehouse | Control Hub: Port 3030 | JupyterLab: Port 8888 | YARN Pool: 3072MB | Cloud: Dataproc 2.1
